_metadata.description: Operator-state write authority: one typed service, field-scoped merges, schema validation before write, and no second authority for any operator decision.

requirements.title: The system shall commit every operator decision through one typed operator-state service that preserves fields it does not own.
requirements.description: Compositional claim for the state domain. Today two authorities exist for resource enablement and a partial writer performs a total write, so the claim is false in both directions.

validation.notes: Evidence target: `internal/operatorstate/service_test.go`; this requirement remains planned until that evidence is added. the shared control-plane service that every writer must route through.

requirements.title: When a surface commits a choice, the operator-state service shall merge only the named fields and shall leave every other field unchanged.
requirements.description: The write API takes a field-scoped patch, not a document. This removes the whole class of defect where a partial writer silently truncates the document, rather than fixing one instance of it by adding a struct field.

validation.notes: Evidence target: `internal/operatorstate/service_test.go`; this requirement remains planned until that evidence is added. a patch that sets one scenario flag changes exactly one field in the written document.

requirements.title: If the stored document carries a field the writing binary does not model, then the write shall preserve that field unchanged.
requirements.description: The regression this pins is live today: a wizard save drops trust_posture and core, which silently disables control-plane core protection and downgrades a shared or hosted install to the personal trust posture. The test uses a document containing every schema field plus one the binary has never seen.

validation.notes: Evidence target: `internal/operatorstate/preserve_test.go`; this requirement remains planned until that evidence is added. round-trips a full document through every writer and asserts byte-for-byte preservation of unowned fields.
Evidence: the HTTP boundary preserves trust_posture and core across a wizard-shaped commit.

requirements.title: Before it writes, the operator-state service shall validate the merged document against operator-state.schema.json and shall reject an invalid write.
requirements.description: The schema sets additionalProperties false, so an invalid write is unrecoverable without hand repair. Validation moves before the write, and the rejection names the failing path.

validation.notes: Evidence target: `internal/operatorstate/service_test.go`; this requirement remains planned until that evidence is added. an out-of-enum trust_posture is rejected and the stored document is untouched.

requirements.title: If any component other than the operator-state service writes the operator-state file, then the repository test suite shall fail.
requirements.description: Enforced structurally with a syntax-aware scan for writes to the operator-state path outside the owning package, so a new writer cannot be introduced quietly.

validation.notes: Evidence target: `internal/operatorstate/single_writer_test.go`; this requirement remains planned until that evidence is added. ast-grep style scan asserting one write site.

requirements.title: The operator-state service shall write the document atomically with secret file permissions.
requirements.description: A partial write leaves an install unbootable. The current implementation already uses the shared atomic writer and the secret permission mode; the target keeps this behaviour when the writer moves into the control plane.

validation.notes: Asserts the written file mode and that a failed encode leaves the prior document intact.

requirements.title: The resource-enable command shall write resource enablement to operator state, and no other file shall carry that decision.
requirements.description: The configuration contract names operator state the source of truth for resource enablement, but the control-plane command writes the repository service manifest instead, and the wizard writes neither. Retiring the second authority is what makes the wizard's resources step meaningful.

validation.notes: Evidence target: `internal/resources/resources_test.go`; this requirement remains planned until that evidence is added. SetEnabled writes operator state and leaves the repository manifest unchanged.

requirements.title: When apply finishes, the service shall record a durable completion marker naming the applied selection and the completion time.
requirements.description: Without a marker, 'this install has been configured' is unobservable: the wizard cannot resume correctly, autoheal cannot tell a fresh host from a configured one, and a desktop first-run cannot decide whether to open setup.

validation.notes: Evidence target: `internal/operatorstate/service_test.go`; this requirement remains planned until that evidence is added. the marker records the applied selection digest and survives a later unrelated patch.

requirements.title: If two surfaces commit different fields at the same time, then both changes shall survive.
requirements.description: A UI toggle and a CLI apply can overlap on the same host. Field-scoped merges under a write lock make the outcome order-independent for disjoint fields.

validation.notes: Evidence target: `internal/operatorstate/concurrency_test.go`; this requirement remains planned until that evidence is added. parallel disjoint patches both land; overlapping patches serialize.

requirements.title: When an operator re-opens the wizard on a configured install, it should load committed state and resume at the first unsatisfied step.
requirements.description: Committed state drives the flow, so the wizard is a re-enterable control surface rather than a one-shot installer. State loading works today; resuming does not, because no completion marker exists and re-entry always lands on the first step.

validation.notes: Asserts committed selections reload on entry; resume-at-step is covered by companion evidence.
Evidence: a configured install with an unmet credential resumes at the credentials step.
